references.text: Joshua reminds the two and a half tribes of Moses' command to help their brothers until they too have found rest and taken possession of the land on the other side of the Jordan.
The Lord has given Israel's brothers rest, and now the tribes who received land east of the Jordan may return to their inheritance that Moses gave them.
Moses' original agreement with Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh that they should help their brothers take possession of the land before returning to their own inheritance.
Moses commands the tribes east of the Jordan to go armed ahead of their brothers, while their families and livestock remain in the cities.
The promise that Israel will have rest from all their enemies when they enter the land the Lord gives them as an inheritance.
The book of Hebrews interprets the rest in the land as a foreshadowing of the spiritual rest that remains for God's people.
